title: design review observations from FCA correctness audit (sutra/102)
description:
Three design observations surfaced during the FCA correctness review (sutra/102). Not bugs — structural limitations worth evaluating.

## O1 — Pairwise-only implication mining

`approximate_implications` discovers single-attribute → single-attribute rules only. Multi-attribute conventions like `{vis:pub, is_async} → returns_result` are structurally undiscoverable. The concept lattice infrastructure exists (`all_concepts`, `next_closure`) but isn't wired into convention mining. Expanding to multi-attribute antecedents would increase expressiveness but risks combinatorial blowup — needs a pruning strategy.

## O2 — Confidence 1.0 lifecycle blind spot

The `confidence < 1.0` filter means the lifecycle system never sees conventions with 100% adherence. The review pipeline still catches first violations (convention materializes at <1.0 at rebuild time), but lifecycle promotion proposals for high-adherence patterns are delayed until the first exception. Small codebases are most affected — a single violation on a 4-symbol pattern drops confidence to 0.75, below the 0.9 threshold, making both convention and violation invisible.

## O3 — No automated forbidden transition signal

`detect_signals` handles descriptive→preferred, preferred→deprecated, deprecated→deleted. The deprecated→forbidden transition has no automated signal — requires manual intervention. This seems intentional (forbidden is a strong assertion) but should be documented explicitly in the lifecycle docs.
execution_record: Closed by evaluation, not code: all three observations resolved by the sutra/176 redesign decision (O1 moot — mining-as-rules retired; O2 fixed — deviation report includes confidence-1.0 patterns; O3 moot — lifecycle machinery deleted, enforcement routes to constraints). See task comment for full verdicts.

messages.author: claude
messages.text:
Evaluated 2026-07-07 during the conventions redesign decision (sutra/176). Verdicts:

O1 (pairwise-only mining): moot. Mining-as-rule-source is being retired; the replacement (diff-scoped deviation reporting) works over the same pairwise statistics. Multi-attribute antecedents over the current vocabulary would only produce more sophisticated noise — revisit only if the attribute vocabulary is enriched (effects, callee patterns) AND the deviation report proves its worth. The identity→obligation attribute typing adopted in the redesign is the pruning strategy this observation asked for.

O2 (confidence<1.0 filter): confirmed harmful, fixed by the redesign. Confidence-1.0 patterns are the *strongest* signal for checking a diff against component norms; the filter in FormalContext::approximate_implications excluded exactly them. Removal is folded into the deviation-report implementation task on the redesign arc.

O3 (no automated deprecated→forbidden signal): moot. The lifecycle/promotion machinery is being deleted entirely (lifetime record across 48 workspaces: 1 accepted proposal vs ~1,500 pending+dismissed, 0 waivers ever). Enforcement routes to hand-written constraint rules instead — forbidden-ness becomes an explicit human declaration in the constraints TOML, which is what O3 concluded it should be.
